title: Englewood neighborhood, violin teacher Professor Scott, the pull of the bass
summary: He describes the country-like town, his violin teacher Professor Scott, and how the sound of the band bassist drew him from the violin to the bass.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: When you were -- what kind of a neighborhood did you grow up in?

Well, a small town, Englewood, right across from New York, you might say. I was brought up in a very country, you know, it was real country out there, and the neighborhood kids -- it was a very nice neighborhood, and of course I friends beautiful, had lots of things. And as I was going along in years and studying the violin, I had a violin teacher whose name was -- I will never forget his name. His name - We used to call him Professor Scott, and he -- he taught me some good things about the fiddle, and I learned pretty good. But I don't -- even until today I don't think I learned too well, because I wasn't really interested in the little violin, especially when I used to listen to the big bands and what have you. Something sort of hit me when I was listening, and I'm sure even up until today that that was the old bass fiddle that the fellows -- the fellow in -- the bassiest in the band was playing, and the sound, it really sounded so good to me that the violin, I didn't even half study it, you know. That's probably the reason why I switched to the bass
